explained.headline: Cyber-attack hits supermarket freezers across seven European countries

happened.text: Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers.
Supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland reported anomalies in their freezer systems.

background.text: This incident follows a similar attack that hit hundreds of French supermarkets in October.
Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, allowing maintenance and troubleshooting to be carried out remotely.
Sabcobel is a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators and operates Delhaize's systems.

matters.text: European Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Christophe Hansen described the attacks as a deliberate attempt to disrupt Europe's food supplies.
Christophe Hansen stated that while food security is not currently at risk, the food waste and impact on businesses are real.
Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away during the previous incident in October.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.
Authorities in the United States are investigating refrigeration malfunctions at American military bases to examine whether they could be linked to the European incidents.
Officials and companies are still working to determine the full scale of the disruptions and whether additional locations have been affected.

terms.definition: An unauthorized digital attempt to access, disrupt or damage computer systems, networks or connected operational technology.
Hardware and software that monitor and control physical devices, machinery and industrial processes.

explained.headline: Russian Strikes Hit Ukrainian Aid Centre and Energy Infrastructure

happened.text: At least 26 people were killed in Russian air strikes targeting a school functioning as an aid distribution centre in the village of Komyshuvakha within the Zaporizhzhia region.
Russian forces also launched a massive overnight attack hitting power generation facilities and substations across multiple Ukrainian regions, including Odesa, Cherkasy, and Kharkiv.
Separate Ukrainian drone attacks caused a fire and injured two employees at an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl.

background.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The latest wave of attacks followed the expiration of a localized six-day humanitarian ceasefire in and around the town of Oleshky in the Kherson region.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy is the president of Ukraine and Steve Witkoff serves as the special envoy for United States President Donald Trump.

matters.text: Steve Witkoff stated that upcoming trilateral discussions in Abu Dhabi between delegations from the United States, Russia and Ukraine will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and next steps toward peace.

US negotiators are also scheduled to meet with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization in Brussels to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine.

European officials announced that a multinational force of about 2,800 troops will hold military exercises in Poland to test how quickly forces can be deployed to support Ukraine once a ceasefire is agreed.

uncertain.text: The sources report that no major breakthrough is expected at the upcoming peace talks.
The sources note that reports regarding specific damage to Russian infrastructure and military facilities could not immediately be independently verified.
The exact terms and final outcomes of any potential future peace deal between Ukraine and Russia remain widely disputed.

A precision-guided munition equipped with aerodynamic wings to allow long-distance gliding towards a target.
Part of an electrical generation, transmission, and distribution system where voltage is transformed.

explained.headline: US plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from trade deal

happened.text: Donald Trump, US president, has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme starting on 1 January 2027.
Jamieson Greer, US Trade Representative, stated that an annual review found both nations engaged in practices inconsistent with the programme's requirements.
The administration cited barriers to trade and investment, corruption concerns in South Africa, and national security and foreign policy interests.

background.text: The African Growth and Opportunity Act allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the United States duty-free.
The announcement follows recent US sanctions against Rwanda's defence ministry over its alleged role in an armed rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

matters.text: Parks Tau said that South Africa will accelerate the diversification of its export markets in order to protect jobs.
South Africa's export-dependent citrus industry warned that its entire value chain across the Atlantic is now under threat.
Leo Brent Bozell III, US Ambassador to South Africa, described the outcome as predictable and preventable.

uncertain.text: Rwanda has denied backing the M23 rebel group despite what the US Treasury described as overwhelming evidence.
Parks Tau described the decision as unfortunate and stated that Washington raised new issues that had not featured in trade negotiations.

terms.definition: Standard trade conditions where member states promise to treat all other members equally without giving preferential tariff rates to specific countries.

removed.text: Cyril Ramaphosa is the President of South Africa, while Parks Tau serves as South Africa's Trade Minister.
why: The provided evidence confirms Cyril Ramaphosa is President, but it does not mention Parks Tau.

explained.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections amid US strikes on Iran

happened.text: Polling stations opened across the United States for midterm elections in which voters are deciding the composition of the entire House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate.
Over 57 million citizens cast early ballots prior to election day.

matters.text: The outcome of the elections will determine the balance of power in Washington for the remainder of Donald Trump's presidential term.

Sources report that if the opposition takes control of either congressional chamber, Donald Trump's presidential authority would be curbed and Democrats could launch investigations into his administration.

uncertain.text: Opinion polls indicate that while Democrats are well-positioned to win the House of Representatives, the race for control of the Senate remains much tighter.

terms.definition: The lower chamber of the United States Congress where states are represented proportionally to their population.
The upper chamber of the United States Congress featuring two members from each state.

removed.text: President Donald Trump's administration has launched an immigration crackdown, imposed tariffs, and engaged in a military conflict with Iran that has contributed to rising living costs.
Sources note it remains unclear when final results will be known, as some closely contested races could take hours or days to resolve.
The United States military carried out strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of the polling.
why: The claim presents the strike as fact, while the evidence identifies it as reported information.

why: Midterm elections occur every two years, not four as stated in the claim.
